run_script: Action: Run a script (plugin run_script, version 1)
With the arguments: ["--", <the delivery's pull_request.number, as a number>]
It runs exactly the bytes checked at the launch (a sealed copy); if the script or its interpreter changes, or the project's folder moves, it asks for your approval again
Runs in /home/op/shop (project p1) as your user op (uid 1000)

Never through a shell: the program is started directly with exactly this argument list. A value from the delivery is one inert argument or variable by construction: never part of another string, never the program or the script, never right after an option

What the program does with an argument is the program's own. BattleLab refuses the positions known to take code: an option's value, and anything before an interpreter's script or program text (python, node, perl, awk, sed, jq, …); it can't know every program
Environment: PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM=dumb, and PR_NUMBER (<the delivery's pull_request.number, as a number>)
Starts with a clean environment: nothing of BattleLab's own is passed on
Stops after 5 minutes; keeps at most 64 KB of stdout and of stderr, with secrets redacted
Secrets never go in as values: a fixed argument or variable that looks like a credential or holds a stored secret is refused, and no stored secret is passed to it
Exit 0 is ok, any other exit code is failed, the time limit is failed; a run cut off by a crash is never run again by itself
Runs only inside a separate process scope (systemd-run --user); without one it is refused. When it ends, everything it started is stopped

What it can reach: everything your user can — your files, your network, your credentials. The project folder is only where it starts and the scope only bounds how long it runs; neither is a filesystem or network sandbox
